solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: We must admit trade is mismanaged in bank?

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so WE takes the rest inside
handled badly, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as printed; it wraps the rest
TRADE IS rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that the trading at a bank has been badly run.
explanation.walkthrough: The bank in the surface is a financial one; the answer is a riverbank, which is why the question mark is there.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a riverbank is one kind of waterside, and the question mark admits the narrowing.

clue.text: One desiring less herb to begin with and more sage

indicators.note: minus, so a letter is taken away
what comes first in herb is its opening letter

blocks.note: one who wishes
first letter of herb, removed from WISHER

explanation.surface: A cook wanting less of one herb and more of the herb sage.
explanation.walkthrough: Herb and sage sit together to suggest the kitchen, but sage here is the adjective, not the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: sage as an adjective means wise, and the comparative matches the -ER ending.

clue.text: Path to secure a victory for Labour

indicators.note: the path holds the other letters fast inside it

blocks.note: a trail is a path
A plus V for victory, placed inside TRAIL

explanation.surface: A political strategy for winning an election for the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital L makes Labour look like the British political party; it is plain hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: travail is painful toil, and labour carries the same sense of hard effort.

clue.text: Rock embracing European form for example

blocks.note: to rock is to roll, as a ship does
standard abbreviation
a mode is a form or manner

explanation.surface: A geology note about rock enclosing a European formation.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock and form suggest geology; rock is really the verb, the side-to-side motion of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense 'someone to follow': setting an example is what a role model does.

clue.text: Unbeatable chorizo served up by Puck?

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means brought upwards, so the letters run bottom to top

blocks.note: Puck is the mischievous sprite in A Midsummer Night's Dream
a Spanish sausage, jokingly 'el banger'; a banger is a sausage

explanation.surface: A menu boast about chorizo served by someone named Puck.
explanation.walkthrough: Chorizo is Spanish, so the setter dresses 'banger' (British slang for a sausage) with the Spanish article EL. The question mark flags both that joke and Puck as a sample imp.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something impregnable cannot be taken or overcome, so it cannot be beaten.

clue.text: Decline leads to everyone being broke

indicators.note: the leading letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: first letters of Everyone Being Broke

explanation.surface: Economic decline leaves everyone short of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as cause and effect in an economy; the clue is only initials after the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym taken from the tide: the ebb is the tide going out, so it stands for any falling away.

clue.text: End of Siegfried in Ring Cycle

indicators.note: take the last letter of Siegfried
that letter goes inside the ring

blocks.note: a ring of bells is a peal
last letter of Siegfried, set inside PEAL

explanation.surface: The final part of Wagner's opera Siegfried within his Ring Cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: Siegfried is the third opera of Wagner's Ring Cycle, so 'Ring Cycle' reads as one title; it splits into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cycle is a verb here, riding a bicycle, and that is done by working the pedals.

clue.text: Greek troops not willing to participate

indicators.note: without, so those letters come away

blocks.note: a platoon is a unit of soldiers
if you're on, you're up for it; removed from PLATOON

explanation.surface: Greek soldiers refusing to join in a campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Greek is the definition on its own: a famous Greek. 'Willing to participate' is ON, as in 'Are you on for tonight?'
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the philosopher is one particular Greek, the nationality standing for the man.

clue.text: Reversing identity, man’s female

indicators.note: turn the letters for identity back to front

blocks.note: ID is short for identity
to man a desk is to staff it

explanation.surface: A gender swap: a man's identity turned round becomes a woman's.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests gender reversal, but man is the verb to staff and the 's is just 'is' joining the parts to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the distaff side of a family is the female line, from the spinning staff women used.

clue.text: Deposit from freemasons close to Craft?

indicators.note: the close, or end, of Craft is its last letter

blocks.note: freemasons meet in lodges, so they are lodge men
last letter of Craft

explanation.surface: Money handed over by freemasons, near to the Craft, as they call freemasonry.
explanation.walkthrough: Freemasons call their movement the Craft, which is why the surface hangs together and why the question mark is there.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from banking: you lodge money with a bank, so the act or sum lodged is a deposit.

clue.text: Leaving a duck, everyone tucks into exclusive seafood

blocks.note: a scoop is an exclusive news story
put inside SCOOP to make SCALLOOP
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O; one O is removed

explanation.surface: A diner skips the duck and everyone digs into a special seafood dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck and tucks into keep us at the dinner table; duck is zero, the cricket score, and exclusive is a journalist's scoop.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the scallop is one shellfish among the many that count as seafood.

clue.text: Slowly stewed beef initially increased in intensity

indicators.note: at the start, so the first letter of beef

blocks.note: first letter of beef
raised = turned up

explanation.surface: A recipe: beef slowly stewed, with the heat turned up at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a cooking instruction, so the definition hides at the front in plain view.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from cooking: braising is slow cooking in a little liquid in a closed pot, close kin to stewing.

clue.text: Field Bernabéu team, missing second half

indicators.note: drop the back half of the name

blocks.note: the Bernabéu is Real Madrid's stadium; its second half ADRID goes

explanation.surface: Real Madrid putting out a side without its second-half players.
explanation.walkthrough: Field reads as the football verb, to put out a team; it is the noun, a sphere of activity.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of a domain of knowledge: someone's field is their realm.

clue.text: Psychic powers in later years keeping old in secret work

blocks.note: extrasensory perception
in age, i.e. when older
standard abbreviation, placed inside INAGE after the I

explanation.surface: Someone who in old age uses their psychic gifts for covert work.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a spy with second sight. The O slips in between the I and the N of IN AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: spying is work done in secret, so the phrase paraphrases the trade.

clue.text: Animal long dead at Clyde port reanimated

indicators.note: brought back to life in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A long-dead creature brought back to life at a Scottish harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Clyde is the river of Glasgow. 'Reanimated' neatly suits a creature long dead, which is what makes the surface work.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the pterodactyl is a flying reptile extinct for millions of years.

clue.text: Creature hunting near ground, moving left to right

indicators.note: L (left) moves from the front to the right-hand end

blocks.note: low = close to the ground; its L goes to the end

explanation.surface: An animal hunting close to the ground, moving across from left to right.
explanation.walkthrough: Left is L, the usual abbreviation, and right means the end of the word. Barn owls hunt by flying low over fields.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the owl is a bird of prey, a creature that hunts.

clue.text: Powerful group of 50 swelling fantastic gay choir

indicators.note: wild, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: GAY CHOIR rearranged
Roman numeral fifty, set inside after the O

explanation.surface: Fifty voices joining a fabulous gay choir makes it a powerful group.
explanation.walkthrough: Of links the definition to the wordplay; 50 is the Roman L, which swells the anagram by one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: an oligarchy is rule by a few, a small group holding power.

clue.text: Writer of Aeneid led astray

indicators.note: gone off course, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The author of Virgil's Aeneid having been misled.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for Virgil, the Aeneid's poet; the 'of' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Defoe, author of Robinson Crusoe, is one writer.

clue.text: Single-minded inspector with Jaguar perhaps in Endeavour

indicators.note: the inspector and the cat go inside the endeavour

blocks.note: a deed is an undertaking or effort
Detective Inspector
a jaguar is a big cat, placed after DI inside DEED

explanation.surface: Inspector Morse, first name Endeavour, famous for driving a Jaguar, is single-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: Endeavour is Inspector Morse's first name and the title of the prequel series, and Morse drove a Jaguar; here it is just an effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone dedicated to a cause is wholly committed, pursuing one aim.

clue.text: True crime work incorporated elderly relatives

blocks.note: Inc. is the abbreviation for incorporated
old = elderly
your blood is your family, as in 'blood is thicker than water'

explanation.surface: A criminal case involving old family members, taken into a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a book title: the answer is the book that founded the true-crime genre.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Truman Capote's 1966 account of a Kansas murder is the classic true-crime book.

clue.text: Willing rider Richard endlessly breaking wind

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: to wind is to coil
Dick, short for Richard, loses its K and goes inside COIL

explanation.surface: A horse-rider called Richard who keeps passing wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Willing rider reads as an eager horseman; wind is the verb, rhyming with find.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a rider is a clause added to a document, and willing means relating to a will, so a rider to a will.

clue.text: Copper beginning to tire in nick

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
first letter of tire

explanation.surface: A police officer beginning to flag in the police station.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper and nick are both British slang from policing (a policeman, a police station), but copper is the metal and nick is a small wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to nick your finger is to cut it slightly, and the noun works the same way.

clue.text: Comfort maiden Zeus seduced for so long

blocks.note: to cheer is to comfort
Io was a mortal woman loved by Zeus in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A young woman consoled after Zeus seduced her for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface dwells on Zeus's affair and makes 'so long' a length of time, but it is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional use: cheerio is a casual British goodbye, just as so long is an informal parting.

clue.text: Constellation also wandered: Alpha moved to the east

indicators.note: east is the right-hand side of a map, so the A goes to the end

blocks.note: and = also
ROAMED with its A (alpha) sent to the end

explanation.surface: A star map note: a constellation drifting, with its brightest star moved eastward.
explanation.walkthrough: Alpha is the NATO word for A, and in an across clue east means to the right, so the A of ROAMED shifts to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Andromeda is one constellation, named after the chained princess of Greek myth.

clue.text: Board somehow communicating green light from Macron, then Merz

blocks.note: French for yes; Macron is the French president
German for yes; Merz is the German chancellor

explanation.surface: A board gives approval passed from Macron to Merz.
explanation.walkthrough: The board's name is French and German yes run together; the definition's second half hints at messages from the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a Ouija board is used at séances, supposedly passing messages from spirits.

clue.text: Best study hard to get grip on English

blocks.note: to cram is to study intensively
standard abbreviation, held inside CRAM

explanation.surface: Advice that the best pupils study hard to master English.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is exam advice; the definition is the noun, the pick of the bunch.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: cream rises to the top of milk, so the cream of any group is its finest part.

clue.text: Density in low cloud that’s thick

blocks.note: mist is cloud at ground level
d is the symbol for density in physics, placed inside MIST

explanation.surface: Thick, dense low cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: Thick suggests dense fog; it is the noun, as in 'in the thick of things'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be in the thick of the action is to be in its midst, its busiest part.

clue.text: Drug lord who ran to restrain murderer

blocks.note: Lord (Sebastian) Coe, Olympic middle-distance runner
Cain killed Abel in Genesis; placed inside COE

explanation.surface: A drug baron trying to hold back a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: Drug lord is a set phrase, but it splits: drug is the definition and lord who ran is Seb Coe, the British runner turned peer.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: cocaine, the stimulant from coca leaves, is one drug.

clue.text: Line this writer grasps when climbing tree

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold in the hand
in a down clue, climbing reads the letters upwards

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself
standard abbreviation, held inside ME

explanation.surface: The writer grabs a rope while climbing a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: This writer is the setter, so ME; the tree is both where the climbing happens and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the elm is one broadleaf tree, once common in English hedgerows.

clue.text: Did coach express disapproval? Nothing revolutionary

blocks.note: tut is the click of the tongue for disapproval
zero
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A question whether the coach tutted, answered with nothing revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Did coach looks like the start of a question; it is the past tense that TUTORED matches.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a coach gives private teaching, which is what a tutor does, and 'did' supplies the past tense.

clue.text: Agent on vacation was resting around Black Sea resort

indicators.note: vacated, emptied of its middle, leaving the outer letters
turned round, so the combined letters run backwards

blocks.note: outer letters of AgenT
past tense of lie; AT + LAY then reversed

explanation.surface: A spy on holiday lounging around a Black Sea resort.
explanation.walkthrough: On vacation reads as holiday, fitting the resort; it is an instruction to empty the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Crimean town, famous for the 1945 Allied conference, is one Black Sea resort.

clue.text: Tactless whisky promotion French king stops

blocks.note: a malt is a malt whisky
an advertisement promotes
French for king; AD ROI goes inside MALT

explanation.surface: A crass whisky advert that a French king puts a stop to.
explanation.walkthrough: Stops reads as the king banning the advert; it works like a cork stopping a bottle, plugging the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: maladroit means clumsy, and in social dealings clumsiness is tactlessness.
